How the model works

Anatomy. Every bone and muscle is a real anatomical surface from BodyParts3D, scaled to a 1.78 m lifter. Leg muscles deform along the paths of a validated musculoskeletal model, so they stretch, shorten and wrap around joints with the motion. Trunk muscles bend with the lumbar spine.

Bar and grip. The bar rests on the upper trapezius, above the shoulder blades and clear of the spine, which is the high-bar position. The hands hold it in a full grip, fingers over the top and thumb around, with the wrists inside their normal range. Forearm and hand muscles follow their bones.

Joints. Hip, knee, patella, ankle and subtalar mechanics come from the Rajagopal full-body OpenSim model with the Lai et al. deep-flexion update. Knee, ankle and subtalar axes were re-fitted to the bone surfaces. With those axes, the knees track over the toes without being forced to.

Motion. The feet are fixed with heels 32 cm apart and toes out 20°. Knee and ankle angles are prescribed. The trunk angle is solved so the combined centre of mass of lifter and bar stays over midfoot, and the lumbar spine gives up about 15° of lordosis at the bottom.

Moments. Joint moments are quasi-static: they come from body and bar weight and the floor reaction, not acceleration. The floor can push each foot inward and twist it, the way lifters “spread the floor”, within friction limits.

Activation. Leg and trunk activation scales each muscle with the joint moment it works against: knee extension for the quadriceps; hip extension for gluteus maximus, adductor magnus and the hamstrings; L5/S1 extension for the back extensors. The scaling is calibrated to published surface EMG from loaded back squats. The vasti are the most active leg muscles, rectus femoris works at about half their level, gluteus maximus and adductor magnus rise steeply with depth, and the hamstrings stay moderate. Lowering a load takes less activation than lifting it, so descent values are about 70% of drive values at the same depth; when paused, drive values are shown. Shoulder, arm and neck values are typical levels for holding a bar, not computed.

Limits. No skin or fat layer is modelled. Muscles can pass through each other where soft tissue would compress in reality. The shoulder blades keep their relaxed standing position rather than being pulled back, and the head stays fixed to the trunk, so the gaze drops as the trunk leans. The centre of pressure is held at midfoot, so the ankle moment barely changes with depth; real lifters shift pressure slightly toward the heel or toes. Activation is an estimate for a lifter working at roughly 70–75% of their best squat, not a measurement.
